## Supervisor v0.10.0

### Marking deadlines
- **When marks are due:** in Settings › Modules & coursework, each coursework now has **Marks due**: a number of weeks after its deadline, or a date. A student with an extension gets their marking date moved on by as many days.
- **Reminders:** the dashboard lists work you haven't marked yet from **3 days** before marks are due, and as overdue once the date has passed. Change the 3 days in Settings › Marking deadlines.
- **Which work:** your own project students' coursework once it is ticked as submitted (and you are one of its markers), and the work of the students you mark without supervising them.
- **MSc dissertations and placement reports:** set one date for all of them in Settings › Marking deadlines. A student with a different date can have their own in their Marking section.
- **In the student's details:** "mark by" appears beside each piece of work you mark, in red once it is late.

### Placement module
- **Set it up once:** add the placement module in Settings › Modules & coursework and tick **Placement** under *Applies to*.
- **Enrolment:** each placement student now has **Enrolled on it** (Unknown, Yes or No). The dashboard reminds you to check it, and flags students who are not enrolled. With more than one placement module, choose each student's.
- **Reminder:** until a placement module is set up, Supervisor reminds you once when it opens, with a button to go to Settings.

### Data files in synced folders (OneDrive, Dropbox)
- **Fewer "Changed somewhere else" warnings:** a sync service sometimes puts back a version of the file that Supervisor saved a moment before. Supervisor now recognises its own earlier saves and saves over them without asking, and says so once.
- **Manual saving:** if the warning keeps coming, it now offers **Save only when I click Save**. The same choice is in Settings › Security. Changes are then saved with the **Save** button at the bottom of the sidebar or Ctrl+S, and when Supervisor locks.
- **Closing with unsaved changes:** with manual saving, closing the window asks whether to **Save and quit**, **Quit without saving** or cancel.

### Size of the interface
- **Size slider:** Settings › Academic year has a **Size** slider, from 60% to 200%. Ctrl + and Ctrl − change it too.
- **Per computer:** the size is kept on each computer, so a 1080p laptop and a large monitor can each have their own.

### A new academic year
- **Start new academic year…** in Settings › Academic year replaces typing the year in. It opens a dialog that sets up the new year in one go.
- **Last year's students:** tick the groups whose year is over (project, placement, advisee and marking students are ticked; research students are not). They are archived, or deleted if you prefer, after a confirmation. A student who also has a role you keep stays. Students archived in earlier years can be deleted at the same time.
- **Dates:** the new semester dates are suggested 52 weeks on, keeping the weekday. Fixed dates (coursework deadlines, marking deadlines, MSc and placement report dates) are listed and can be moved on 52 weeks, cleared or kept.
- **A way back:** the data as it was is saved first and kept as the .bak, until you next click Save or unlock again.

### Choosing dates
- **One click:** clicking a day in the calendar of any date field (meetings, deadlines, extensions, visits, settings) now sets it straight away and closes the calendar. There is no Save button to press any more.
- **Clicking elsewhere** or pressing Esc closes the calendar without changing the date. Moving between months with the arrows doesn't change it either.
- **Today:** today's date is outlined, and **Today** picks it.

### Fixes
- **Quit without saving:** choosing it after a failed save no longer tries to save once more on the way out.

### Notes
- Existing data files open unchanged. Marking deadlines start unset, so there are no reminders until you set them.
